summary: Michiel de Vaan specializes in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his doctoral studies under Alexander Lubotsky (~1998–2002) and held a post at Leiden University from around 2002 to 2014.

A Buddhist studies scholar educated at Taisho University, Michihiko Komine served there as an assistant (attested 1978–1980) and professor (~1993–2016). He also held posts at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014) and the Japanese Association for Esoteric Buddhist Studies (attested 2015).

Michihiko Yajima works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied as a graduate student at the University of Tokyo (attested 1981), where he later held a post (attested 1992), and served as a professor at Tsurumi Women's University (attested 2003).

Michihiro Ikeda is a scholar in Buddhist studies. His career includes posts as a lecturer at Setagaya Gakuen High School (attested 1996) and Komazawa Junior College (attested 2005), as well as librarian at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2005–2006).

Michiko Yusa works in religious studies, philosophy, and Japanology. She completed her doctoral studies under Raimon Panikkar at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1978–1983) and served as a professor in the Department of Foreign Languages at Western Washington University (~1983–2021).
Michio Kamikawa was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Ritsumeikan University and held a post at Aichi Prefectural University (attested 2016).

Michio Yano works in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University and Brown University under David Pingree, Frits Staal, and Kiyoshi Yabuuchi. He lectured at Kyoto University and served as a professor at Kyoto Sangyo University (1973–2015).

Michitoshi Barada specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied under Jien Abe and J. R. Joshi. He held posts at Otani University (attested 1992), the Eastern Institute (attested 2000), and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2000–2003, 2026).
Michiya Ito studied as a graduate student at Tohoku University (attested 1990). He also held posts at Tohoku University (attested 1990 and 2001–2004).

Michiyo Hoshi works in Tibetology and linguistics. She held posts at the Research Institute for Languages and Cultures of Asia and Africa as a collaborative researcher and at Toyo Bunko as a researcher (attested 2003).
Midori Nishino is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She pursued doctoral studies at Taisho University (attested 2006) and later worked there as a researcher (attested 2010–2015).
Mieko Kajihara is an Indologist who studied under Michael Witzel (attested 1997) and earned her PhD from Harvard University by 2002.

Migmar Tsering worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studying under Khenpo Appey Rinpoche. He served at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1990), headed Sakya College (attested 1991–2003), and was affiliated with the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2006).
Miguel de Unamuno was a philosopher who studied at Universidad Central (~1880–1884). He spent his academic career at the University of Salamanca (~1891–1936).

Mihai Eminescu was active in Indology and other fields. He studied at Staatsgymnasium Czernowitz, the University of Vienna (1869–1872), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1872–1874), where he studied under Albrecht Weber.

Mihai Șora was a philosopher who studied under Mircea Eliade at the University of Bucharest (~1934–1938), later studying at the University of Paris and CNRS. He held a post at the State Publishing House for Literature and Arts (~1951–1969).
Mihail Alekseevič Širjaev was an Indologist who studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy and Aleksej Petrovič Barannikov. He served as a Docent of Indology at the Leningrad Oriental Institute.

Mihail Nikolaevič Sotnikov worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as Docent of Indology at the Leningrad Oriental Institute, Head of Indian Linguistics at MGIMO (1954–1956), and held a post at Moscow State University (1956–1965).

Mikael Aktor works in religious studies and Indology, earning a PhD from the University of Copenhagen (1998). He held posts at Copenhagen (attested 1995–1997), Aarhus University (attested 1997–1999), and became an Associate Professor at the University of Southern Denmark (1999).

Mikaël Bauer specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Kanazawa University under Paul Hoornaert and Noritoshi Aramaki, and earned a PhD at Harvard under Ryuichi Abe (attested 2010). He is an Associate Professor at McGill University (attested 2026).
